notes.text: A vision appeared to Paul by night — It was not a dream, though it was by night. No other dream is mentioned in the New Testament than that of Joseph and of Pilate's wife. A man of Macedonia - Probably an angel clothed in the Macedonian habit, or using the language of the country, and representing the inhabitants of it. Help us - Against Satan, ignorance, and sin.

We sought to go into Macedonia — This is the first place in which St. Luke intimates his attendance on the apostle. And here he does it only in an oblique manner. Nor does he throughout the history once mention his own name, or any one thing which he did or said for the service of Christianity; though Paul speaks of him in the most honourable terms, Colossians iv, 14; 2 Tim. iv, 11; and probably as the brother whose praise in the Gospel went through all the Churches, 2 Cor. viii, 18. The same remark may be made on the rest of the sacred historians, who every one of them show the like amiable modesty.
We ran with a straight course — Which increased their confidence that God had called them.

The first city — Neapolis was the first city they came to in that part of Macedonia which was nearest to Asia: in that part which was farthest from it, Philippi. The river Strymon ran between them. Philippi was a Roman colony.

We went out of the gate — The Jews usually held their religious assemblies (either by choice or constraint) at a distance from the heathens: by a river side - Which was also convenient for purifying themselves. Where prayer was wont to be made - Though it does not appear there was any house built there. We spake - At first in a familiar manner. Paul did not immediately begin to preach.

A worshipper of God — Probably acquainted with the prophetic writings whose heart the Lord opened - The Greek word properly refers to the opening of the eyes: and the heart has its eyes, Eph. i, 18. These are closed by nature and to open them is the peculiar work of God.

She was baptized and her family — Who can believe that in so many families there was no infant? Or that the Jews, who were so long accustomed to circumcise their children, would not now devote them to God by baptism? She entreated us - The souls of the faithful cleave to those by whom they were gained to God. She constrained us - By her importunity. They did not immediately comply, lest any should imagine they sought their own profit by coming into Macedonia.

glossa.text:
*A man of Macedonia.* The angel of that nation likened to a man of Macedonia, by the property of the tongue, or by a special form, or by the judgment of the word.

*Help us. ((RAB.))* This was said in the person of a man, for angels do not need human help. Or the angel says this on account of those over whom he presides, that they may be baptized and be saved.

*Help us.* He shows that the Macedonians, or the angels, are inspired by God, or that certain teachers had begun to be taught.
*Samothracia.* Thracia, Neapolis and Philippi are cities.
*Certain days, conferring.* In certain books is found: Conferring the word of the Lord on the sabbath day.

*A seller of purple.* A queen clothed in royal purple, or a weaver of purple, or one selling purple, signifies the Church which sells purple while she pours out blood for Christ, that life may be purchased. Purple rightly designates blood by its colour and by its nature, because it is made from the blood of shellfish. Lydda compelled the apostle, with his companions, to enter her house: because the Church received with a devout heart the preaching rejected by the Jews.
*She constrained us. ((RAB.))* Here is given an example, or two examples are given: one of constraining guests, the other of entering in to the newly converted.

notes.text: Thy way — The way of truth, or the true religion; the same which in the next clause is called his saving health, and both together signify the way of salvation; deal so graciously with thy people, that thereby the Gentile-world may at last be allured to join with them.
Judge — Rule them. Govern - Hebrew. lead; gently, as a shepherd doth his sheep; and not rule them with rigor, as other lords had done.

Them — When the people of the earth shall be converted to God, God will cause it to yield them abundance of all sorts of fruits. Under which one blessing, all other blessings both temporal and spiritual are comprehended. Our own - He who is Israel's God in a peculiar manner. The occasion of this psalm, seems to have been David's translation of the ark to Zion, which was managed with great solemnity and devotion. For the first words are the very same which Moses appointed for such occasions, Num. x, 35, and the following verses pursue the same matter. Thence he falls into a description of some of the glorious works of the God to whom this ark belonged. But because David knew that both himself and the ark were types of Christ, and that the church of Israel were a type of the catholick church, consisting of Jews and Gentiles, and that the legal administrations were types of those of the gospel, he therefore by the spirit of prophecy, looked through the types, to the great mysteries of Christ's resurrection and ascension, and of the special privileges of the Christian church, and of the conversion of the Gentiles, and intermixes passages, which immediately belong to these things, although the words be so ordered, that they carry a manifest allusion to the present actions, and may be applied to them, in a secondary sense. He first prays against God's enemies, and for his people, ver. 1-3. Then praises God, for his greatness and goodness, ver. 4-6. For his wonderful works, ver. 7-14. For his special presence in his church, ver. 15- 17. The ascension of Christ, and the salvation of his people, ver. 18-20. His victories over his enemies, and favours to his church, ver. 21-28. The accession of the Gentiles to the church, ver. 29- 31. An awful acknowledgment of the glory and grace of God, ver. 32-35. To the chief musician, A psalm or song of David.

glossa.text: *May God have mercy. ((Ibid.))* The blessing of God is first, which is as it were a rain watering the earth of our mind: thence we bless him, which is as it were the fruit; and in both it is we that grow, not he. Let him therefore who desires the rain of the Lord's blessing say: May God have mercy on us, etc. *May God have mercy on us and bless us.* ((CAS.)) But many who wish, etc., *as far as* and because Christ is known among the nations: *Let them confess,* etc. *May he bless us. ((Ibid.))* The Creator blesses the creature, by multiplying it, in number and in merit. The creature blesses the Creator, by praising him with heart, voice and work, and by ascribing to him every good thing that it has.
*Let the peoples confess to thee, O God. ((Ibid.))* After knowledge he exhorts them to confess, for direction and for judgment.
*Let them be glad and rejoice.* ((AUG.)) Because, having now confessed, they do not fear the judgments to come, to whom Christ is an advocate, not a judge, *let them be glad.*

*Let the peoples confess to thee, O God.* ((CAS.)) The same admonition, tending to another thing, because the earth has given her fruit, and although the beginning of the sense is the same, yet it tends to different things.

*The earth hath given her fruit.* ((HIER.)) To Mary, Christ, etc., *as far as:* But not she alone owes this, nay rather, *let him bless* also *us. God, our God. ((Ibid.))* Three times, the Trinity, *him,* the unity. *And let them fear him.* ((CAS.)) Fear is asked for in the midst of benefits, that what is entrusted may be warily kept: the fear of God begins and completes; he who has learned to fear does not cease to love.

notes.text: And he carried me away in the spirit — The same expression as before, chap. xvii, 3. And showed me the holy city Jerusalem - The old city is now forgotten, so that this is no longer termed the new, but absolutely Jerusalem. O how did St. John long to enter in! but the time was not yet come. Ezekiel also describes "the holy city," and what pertains thereto, xl.-xlviii. Ezek. xl, 1-Ezek. xlviii, 35 but a city quite different from the old Jerusalem, as it was either before or after the Babylonish captivity. The descriptions of the prophet and of the apostle agree in many particulars; but in many more they differ. Ezekiel expressly describes the temple, and the worship of God therein, closely alluding to the Levitical service. But St. John saw no temple, and describes the city far more large, glorious, and heavenly than the prophet. Yet that which he describes is the same city; but as it subsisted soon after the destruction of the beast. This being observed, both the prophecies agree together and one may explain the other.

glossa.text: *Into a great mountain.* Christ is the *mountain*, because he is the defence of his own, he is great, because he fills the whole world, *high,* because unconquerable. *He showed me the city.* And upon that mountain he showed the foundation of the Church.

notes.text: Jesus answered — Because ye love and obey me, and they do not, therefore I will reveal myself to you, and not to them. My Father will love him - The more any man loves and obeys, the more God will love him. And we will come to him, and make our abode with him - Which implies such a large manifestation of the Divine presence and love, that the former in justification is as nothing in comparison of it.

In my name — For my sake, in my room, and as my agent. He will teach you all things - Necessary for you to know. Here is a clear promise to the apostles, and their successors in the faith, that the Holy Ghost will teach them all that truth which is needful for their salvation.

Peace I leave with you — Peace in general; peace with God and with your own consciences. My peace - In particular; that peace which I enjoy, and which I create, I give - At this instant. Not as the world giveth - Unsatisfying unsettled, transient; but filling the soul with constant, even tranquillity. Lord, evermore give us this peace! How serenely may we pass through the most turbulent scenes of life, when all is quiet and harmonious within! Thou hast made peace through the blood of thy cross. May we give all diligence to preserve the inestimable gift inviolate, till it issue in everlasting peace!
God the Father is greater than I — As he was man. As God, neither is greater nor less than the other.
I have told you — Of my going and return.

glossa.text: *We will come to him.* God comes to man, while man comes to God. Man comes by believing, obeying, beholding, receiving; God comes by succouring, enlightening, filling. *And a mansion,* etc. Charity makes [a man] dwell in the house in which the Father and the Son make a mansion, whence he will also give the manifestation concerning which that man had asked.

*These things have I spoken to you.* These things concerning the mansion in those who love him, in which is signified the future spiritual Church, in which are the blessed, from whom he does not withdraw. *Abiding with you.* Here [is] the present bodily Church, in which he visits by delivering, and returns.

*The Paraclete.* Although to console is the work of the Trinity, yet it pertains most of all to the person of the Holy Spirit, because in Scripture the Holy Spirit is designated by the name of goodness: through goodness therefore God consoles us, through it he bestows on us all his good things.

*He you.* Because even though the Son teaches us and reveals the Father, he does all this through his goodness. *He shall teach you all things.* He shall teach the things that I shall have said, not that the Son says and the Spirit teaches, because what he says and teaches, the Trinity itself also says and teaches. But because it is a Trinity, it behoves the single persons to be intimated, whom we ought to hear distinctly, to understand inseparably. When therefore we say, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, we do not say them at the same time, since they cannot be not at the same time.

*Peace I leave with you.* Being about to go to the Father. *Peace,* etc. And repeating concerning the same. *My peace I give.* And this is what the Prophet says: *Peace upon peace ((Isa. XXVII))*. There is a peace in this world, abiding in which we conquer the enemy, love one another, and do not judge one another concerning hidden things. There will be a peace in the world to come when we shall reign without an enemy, where one will not be able to dissent from another, where *all things are open and praise is to each one ((I Cor. IV))*. But in him and from him is each peace. *For he himself is our peace ((Ephes. II))*, and we believe him, because he is, and we shall see him as he is. Whence what he says, my, from the latter is to be understood also of the former. Or, the peace in this world is ours, which is some [peace] and not full; and from him in the world to come is his own peace, where nothing is repugnant, in the manner in which he himself has it.

*Let it not be troubled.* Because I leave you in peace, let not your heart be troubled at that which I said, I go, as though at the shepherd's absence the wolf invades; because as man I go, as God I am present.

*If you loved. ((AUG.))* This was to go to him, and to withdraw from us, etc., *as far as* that incorruptible dust might sit at the right hand of the Father.

*You would rejoice,* etc. Because human nature is to be congratulated, which is raised to the right hand of the Father, in whom the rest hope for the same for themselves.

hymns.title: Sois la semilla gue ha de crecer (You are the seed that will grow a new sprout)
At the font we start our journey
O God be gracious to us and bless us
All creatures of our God and King
We are marching in the light of God

echoes.text: God spoke to Israel in the visions of the night, and said, “Jacob, Jacob!” He said, “Here I am.” He said, “I am God, the God of your father. Don’t be afraid to go down into Egypt, for there I will make of you a great nation. I will go down with you into Egypt. I will also surely bring you up again. Joseph will close your eyes.”
echoes.note: God speaks to Israel/Jacob 'in visions of the night,' directing his movement to a new land ('I will go down with thee') with assurance of divine purpose. The Macedonian vision in the night that redirects Paul's journey across into Europe shares the genre (night vision) and function (divine redirection of geography) closely.

echoes.text: Yahweh went before them by day in a pillar of cloud, to lead them on their way, and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light, that they might go by day and by night:
echoes.note: The Spirit twice forbidding and not allowing the missionaries' chosen routes, then steering them, echoes the pillar of cloud and fire guiding Israel's route step by step; divine micromanagement of the missionary itinerary as a new wilderness leading. Thematic only.

echoes.text: After these things Yahweh’s word came to Abram in a vision, saying, “Don’t be afraid, Abram. I am your shield, your exceedingly great reward.”
echoes.note: 'A vision appeared to Paul in the night' uses the stock revelatory idiom of the word/vision of the LORD coming in the night; Abram's night vision is the paradigm of God commissioning through nocturnal revelation. Generic verbal resonance.

echoes.text: Then was the secret revealed to Daniel in a vision of the night. Then Daniel blessed the God of heaven.
echoes.note: Mystery 'revealed in a night vision' as the medium of divine disclosure; faint Septuagintal parallel for night-vision revelation that resolves a course of action.

echoes.text: Yahweh your God will circumcise your heart, and the heart of your seed, to love Yahweh your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, that you may live.
echoes.note: 'The Lord opened her heart to listen' is the divine-initiative idiom of the LORD circumcising/opening the heart so that Israel will hear and obey; conversion is portrayed as God's sovereign opening of the heart, the inward counterpart to covenant circumcision. Thematic coherence strong.

echoes.text: She makes for herself carpets of tapestry. Her clothing is fine linen and purple.
echoes.note: Lydia, a 'seller of purple' whose household and hospitality she manages, evokes the capable woman of Proverbs 31 whose clothing is purple and who trades in fine cloth; a wealthy, industrious, God-honoring matron. Suggestive characterization, no quotation.

echoes.text: blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats’ hair,
echoes.note: Purple as the prized textile of the tabernacle offerings; Lydia's trade in purple carries an aura of dignity and devoted craft. Lexical (purple) only.

echoes.text: Open my eyes, that I may see wondrous things out of your law.
echoes.note: 'Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things' as the prayer-paradigm for God enabling perception of his word; Lydia's opened heart to attend to Paul's words is its narrative fulfillment. Conceptual parallel.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

spans.label: Second journey
spans.note: Split with Barnabas; took Silas, picked up Timothy and Luke. Crossed into Europe at the Macedonian call — the Philippian jailer, the Areopagus, and a year and a half building the church at Corinth.

places.name: Troas
places.id: Alexandria Troas on the Aegean coast of Mysia, founded by Antigonus c. 310 B.C. and refounded by Lysimachus. A Roman colony from c. 12 B.C. The natural embarkation port for crossings to Macedonia. Distinct from the Homeric Troy / Hisarlik some 30 km to the north.

places.name: Macedonia
places.id: The Roman province (formed 146 B.C.) covering northern Greece, the Vardar/Axios valley, and adjacent territories. Capital at Thessalonica from 27 B.C. The 'Macedonian vision' of Acts 16:9 brings the gospel into Europe for the first time.

places.name: Samothrace
places.id: A small mountainous island in the northern Aegean, c. 60 km off the Thracian coast. Famous in antiquity for the Sanctuary of the Great Gods (the Cabeiroi); the Hellenistic Winged Victory of Samothrace was carved here. The standard overnight stop for ships crossing from Troas to Neapolis.

places.name: Neapolis
places.id: On the Macedonian coast c. 14 km southeast of Philippi, modern Kavala. The harbor served Philippi and was the standard western terminus of the sea route from Asia Minor.

places.name: Philippi
places.id: On a hill above the Egnatian Way c. 14 km inland from Neapolis, refounded by Philip II of Macedon (hence the name) on the older site of Krenides. A Roman colony (Colonia Augusta Iulia Philippensis) from 42 B.C. after the battle of Philippi where Antony and Octavian defeated Brutus and Cassius. The 'foremost city of the district' in v. 16:12.

places.name: Thyatira
places.id: Modern Akhisar in western Anatolia (Roman Asia), a centre of guild industry famous for purple-dye production (cf. Lydia, the ‘seller of purple’, v. 16:14). One of the seven cities addressed in Revelation 2:18-29.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: In the visions of God brought he me into the land of Israel, and set me down on a very high mountain, whereon was as it were the frame of a city on the south.
echoes.note: 'He carried me away in the Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the holy city' (v.10) closely reproduces Ezekiel's visionary transport: 'he brought me... and set me upon a very high mountain, on which was the frame of a city.' Tour-of-the-city framework derives directly from Ezek 40-48.

echoes.text: These are the exits of the city: On the north side four thousand and five hundred reeds by measure; and the gates of the city shall be after the names of the tribes of Israel, three gates northward: the gate of Reuben, one; the gate of Judah, one; the gate of Levi, one. At the east side four thousand and five hundred reeds, and three gates: even the gate of Joseph, one; the gate of Benjamin, one; the gate of Dan, one. At the south side four thousand and […]
echoes.note: Twelve gates inscribed with the names of the twelve tribes, three on each of the four sides (v.12-13), reproduces Ezekiel's gate-list (three N, three E, three S, three W, named for the tribes). Highest structural and verbal correspondence for the gates.

echoes.text: “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and Yahweh’s glory is risen on you. For, behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the peoples; but Yahweh will arise on you, and his glory shall be seen on you.
echoes.note: 'Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you' underlies 'having the glory of God. Her light was like a most precious stone' (v.11). Isa 60 is the controlling intertext for the city's radiance and is quarried throughout 21:23-26.

echoes.text: I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
echoes.note: Bridal imagery resumed (v.9 'the wife, the Lamb's bride') — cf. 21:2; the bride 'adorned' theme carries into the jewel-glory description (v.11).

echoes.text: Behold, the glory of the God of Israel came from the way of the east: and his voice was like the sound of many waters; and the earth shined with his glory. It was according to the appearance of the vision which I saw, even according to the vision that I saw when I came to destroy the city; and the visions were like the vision that I saw by the river Chebar; and I fell on my face. Yahweh’s glory came into the house by the way of the gate whose prospect is […]
echoes.note: 'The glory of the God of Israel... the earth shone with his glory' as it enters the temple-city — parallels the city 'having the glory of God' (v.11). Reinforces the Ezekielian glory-filling pattern.

echoes.text: “You afflicted, tossed with storms, and not comforted, behold, I will set your stones in beautiful colors, and lay your foundations with sapphires. I will make your pinnacles of rubies, and your gates of sparkling jewels, and all your walls of precious stones.
echoes.note: Jerusalem rebuilt with sapphires, jewels, and precious-stone gates — anticipates the jasper radiance (v.11) and is the chief source for the foundations/gates jewelry developed in 21:18-21.

echoes.text: The stones shall be according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names; like the engravings of a signet, everyone according to his name, they shall be for the twelve tribes.
echoes.note: The high priest's breastpiece bearing the names of the twelve tribes engraved on twelve stones (v.12 'names of the twelve tribes') — links the tribe-inscribed gates to priestly typology; develops fully at 21:19-20.

echoes.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying, “The children of Israel shall encamp every man by his own standard, with the banners of their fathers’ houses: at a distance from the Tent of Meeting shall they encamp around it.” Those who encamp on the east side toward the sunrise shall be of the standard of the camp of Judah, according to their divisions: and the prince of the children of Judah shall be Nahshon the son of Amminadab. His division, and those […]
echoes.note: The wilderness camp arranged by tribes three-per-side around the tabernacle on the four compass points — pattern behind the three-gates-per-side arrangement (v.13).

echoes.text: Behold, a wall on the outside of the house all around, and in the man’s hand a measuring reed six cubits long, of a cubit and a hand breadth each: so he measured the thickness of the building, one reed; and the height, one reed.
echoes.note: The wall surrounding the temple-complex measured by the angel — anticipates the 'great and high wall' (v.12) and the measuring of 21:15-17.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: I will set my tent among you, and my soul won’t abhor you. I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you will be my people.
echoes.note: 'I will make my dwelling among you... and I will walk among you and be your God' is the covenant indwelling formula that 14:23 personalizes: 'we will come to him and make our home (monen) with him.' High Coherence because John reuses the same divine-dwelling-with-the-people promise, now realized as Father and Son abiding with the believer.

echoes.text: My tent also shall be with them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
echoes.note: 'My dwelling place shall be with them, and I will be their God,' the new-covenant restatement of God dwelling among his people, reinforces the indwelling promise of 14:23. Recurrence of the 'dwelling with them' formula (Lev/Ezek) strengthens Volume; medium because John gives the topos individual rather than national scope.

echoes.text: Sing and rejoice, daughter of Zion; for, behold, I come, and I will dwell in your midst,’ says Yahweh. Many nations shall join themselves to Yahweh in that day, and shall be my people; and I will dwell in your midst, and you shall know that Yahweh of Armies has sent me to you.
echoes.note: 'I will dwell in your midst... and many nations shall join themselves to the LORD... and shall be my people,' an eschatological in-dwelling promise resonant with the Father and Son making their home with the one who loves Jesus. Low confidence: it adds Recurrence to the divine-indwelling motif but contributes no distinctive wording to 14:23.

echoes.text: These words, which I command you this day, shall be on your heart;
echoes.note: 'These words that I command you... shall be on your heart,' the Shema's call to internalize God's word, undergirds 14:23-24's 'keep my word'/'the word you hear is the Father's.' Low and contested: the keep-the-word idiom is broadly Deuteronomic and not anchored to a single verse here.

echoes.text: ‘Yahweh bless you, and keep you. Yahweh make his face to shine on you, and be gracious to you. Yahweh lift up his face toward you, and give you peace.’
echoes.note: The Aaronic blessing climaxes 'the LORD... give you peace (shalom),' the priestly bestowal of divine peace that Jesus reissues as 'Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you.' High Coherence: Jesus speaks the priestly gift-of-peace formula directly, distinguishing his giving from the world's, just as the blessing conveys God's own peace.

echoes.text: You will keep whoever’s mind is steadfast in perfect peace, because he trusts in you.
echoes.note: 'You keep him in perfect peace whose mind is stayed on you,' linking peace with an untroubled, trusting heart, parallels 14:27's 'my peace I give... let not your heart be troubled.' Coherence is strong between the peace-and-undisturbed-heart pairing; medium because the connection is thematic rather than a verbal citation.

echoes.text: I create the fruit of the lips: Peace, peace, to him who is far off and to him who is near,” says Yahweh; “and I will heal them.”
echoes.note: 'Peace, peace, to the far and to the near, says the LORD; and I will heal him' is God's gift of peace to his people, the prophetic backdrop to Jesus bestowing his own peace. Medium for the shared divine-gift-of-peace motif; John heightens it by contrasting Jesus' peace with the world's hollow giving.

echoes.text: ‘The latter glory of this house will be greater than the former,’ says Yahweh of Armies; ‘and in this place will I give peace,’ says Yahweh of Armies.”
echoes.note: 'In this place I will give peace, declares the LORD of hosts,' tying peace to the eschatological house/temple, resonates with the farewell peace given amid the 'Father's house' discourse. Low confidence: a thematic temple-peace link rather than a verbal one, supplementing the stronger Aaronic and Isaianic echoes.

echoes.text: The Spirit of Yahweh will rest on him: the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahweh.
echoes.note: The resting 'Spirit of wisdom and understanding' that teaches and counsels stands behind the Paraclete who 'will teach you all things' (14:26). Low and contested here because the teaching-Spirit link is better located at 14:17; included for the instructive-Spirit motif that the reminder-and-teaching function of the Counselor presupposes.

echoes.text: You gave also your good Spirit to instruct them, and didn’t withhold your manna from their mouth, and gave them water for their thirst.
echoes.note: 'You gave your good Spirit to instruct them,' a rare OT statement of the Spirit as teacher of God's people, parallels the Paraclete who 'will teach you all things.' Low confidence: genuine conceptual match for the teaching-Spirit, but verbally remote and not signaled as a source by John.

echoes.text: You shall love Yahweh your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your might.
echoes.note: 'You shall love the LORD your God' lies behind 14:28's 'if you loved me' and 14:31's 'that the world may know that I love the Father,' transposing the Shema's love onto the Father-Son relation. Low and contested: it reiterates the Deuteronomic love idiom already credited at 14:15, here governing Jesus' own filial love.

echoes.text: Now this is the commandment, the statutes, and the ordinances, which Yahweh your God commanded to teach you, that you might do them in the land where you go over to possess it;
echoes.note: 'The commandment... that the LORD commanded me to teach you' models the obedient mediator who does only as God commanded, the pattern Jesus claims in 14:31, 'as the Father commanded me, so I do.' Low confidence: the as-commanded obedience motif is generically Deuteronomic, supplying coloring rather than a specific source.

echoes.text: He laid his hands on him, and commissioned him, as Yahweh spoke by Moses.
echoes.note: Moses commissions Joshua 'as the LORD directed... so he did,' the do-as-commanded formula echoed in Jesus' 'as the Father commanded me, even so I do.' Low and contested: a faint obedient-agent parallel without verbal anchoring; one of several Pentateuchal 'as commanded, so he did' instances.

echoes.text: I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.”
echoes.note: The protoevangelium's enmity between the serpent and the woman's seed faintly underlies 'the ruler of this world comes, and he has nothing in me,' where the satanic adversary advances but holds no claim on Jesus. Figural and contested: John's 'ruler of this world' draws on a Second-Temple satanology more than on a single Genesis verse, so the link is thematic.

echoes.text: Now on the day when God’s sons came to present themselves before Yahweh, Satan also came among them. Yahweh said to Satan, “Where have you come from?” Then Satan answered Yahweh, and said, “From going back and forth in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.” Yahweh said to Satan, “Have you considered my servant, Job? For there is no one like him in the earth, a blameless and an upright man, one who fears God, and turns away from evil.” Then Satan […]
echoes.note: The Adversary (ha-satan) who roams the earth and is granted limited power over the righteous supplies an OT antecedent for 'the ruler of this world' who comes but 'has nothing in' Jesus. Low confidence: it grounds the accusing-adversary figure conceptually, but John's title and the 'no claim on me' idea outrun anything verbal in Job.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Christ is risen!
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you.
Let not your hearts be troubled or afraid.
Those who love me will keep my word, and we will come and make our home with them.
The Father will send the Spirit to teach us all things.
Come to the city of light, the river of life, the tree whose leaves heal the nations.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Imagine a city where the gates never close and the night never falls, because the Lamb himself is its light.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
Down its main street runs a river bright as crystal, and on the banks a tree whose leaves are for the healing of the nations.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
And the One who makes that home says to you now: Peace I leave with you; do not let your hearts be afraid.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
Those who love me will keep my word, and the Father and I will come and make our home with them.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
So bring your troubled heart to the river and the light:
Christ is risen, Alleluia!

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Peace I leave with you; do not be afraid.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
Those who love me, my Father and I will make our home with them.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
A river of life runs through the city, the tree healing the nations.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
Come to the light that never fails; let us worship.
Christ is risen, Alleluia!
